Jun 23, 2026 · Marc DeBevoise has been appointed CEO of OverDrive, succeeding founder Steve Potash in the role, the digital content provider announced today. The leadership transition was planned and is “designed to support OverDrive's continued growth and global expansion," per an announcement. "Founding and building OverDrive has been the most rewarding journey of my career," said Potash, who will stay on as chairman of the board, said in a statement. "With Marc leading as CEO, the company is exceptionally well positioned to grow and evolve. As Chairman, I look forward to supporting Marc and our team while continuing to champion the libraries, schools, and institutions at the heart of our mission." hits.title: OverDrive Founder Steve Potash Steps Back; Marc DeBevoise Takes Over as CEO
hits.snippet: OverDrive founder Steve Potash (l) and newly appointed CEO Marc DeBevoise. It's the end of an era at leading library vendor OverDrive. On June 23, the company announced that the company's founder and visionary Steve Potash has stepped back from his role as CEO, handing the reins to Marc DeBevoise, who joined the company roughly four months ago as President. "OverDrive has extraordinary reach, incredible momentum, and an enduring mission—and I’m thrilled to lead this company forward," DeBevoise said. "I'm grateful to Steve for his continued partnership and to the Board for their confidence, and I look forward to working with our team and partners to build on everything this company stands for." The move comes just days ahead of the 2026 American Library Association Annual Conference, set to run from June 25-30 in Chicago, and as the library ebook market has entered a contentious new period, with several states and municipalities considering—and three so far passing—legislation designed to rein in what librarians say are unsustainable prices and license terms from the major publishers. hits.snippet: # We do the hardest part of sales Local media needs more local direct revenue than ever. But the old way of generating it doesn’t work like it used to. By Chris Overby, Founder & CEO, OverDrive Group · July 2026 If you’ve been leading local media sales teams over the past few decades like I have, you’ve watched the job get harder. We need more local direct revenue than ever. National and regional dollars have shifted toward programmatic and digital platforms, and what’s left has to be built locally, one business at a time. At the same time, there are fewer people doing that work. More than half of broadcast sellers have left the industry over the last decade, and the sellers still here are carrying more accounts, more responsibility, and less time to go find new business. The old junior AE model doesn’t work like it used to either. Hiring young sellers to pound the phones, build a book, and earn their way up used to help fill the top of the funnel. But that job isn’t as attractive as it once was. The people who would’ve taken those roles ten years ago now have better options in digital and tech sales, and they’re taking them. hits.title: OverDrive Taps Digital Strategy Expert Marc DeBevoise
hits.snippet: Digital content provider OverDrive announced on March 3 that it has brought in Marc DeBevoise as its new president. DeBevoise, former CEO at the video platform Brightcove and a past leader at the online content network CBS Interactive, will help guide the company known for library reading app Libby, school “science of reading app” Sora, and video-streaming app Kanopy. OverDrive founder and CEO Steve Potash, who served as company president prior to DeBevoise’s appointment, [said in a statement](https://company.overdrive.com/2026/03/03/overdrive-names-marc-debevoise-president-expanding-support-for-libraries-and-schools/) that he expects DeBevoise to “make Libby, Sora, and Kanopy even more user friendly, more inclusive, and more joyful to use” and “help libraries and schools do what they do best, change lives through reading, viewing, and learning.” Potash and DeBevoise now will work together with the OverDrive leadership team.
